marks.gloss_en: baraita: a woman's gett found in the market is returned to the wife when the husband admits it -- with no stated time limit
mishna (20a): any court enactment that is found is returned -- Rabba's ground for returning the court gett
Rabba ruled in practice, per his own teaching, that the gett found at the Pumbedita flax-house be returned
version 1: it was found where flax is SOLD -- caravans frequent, but no two identical couples established
version 2: it was found where flax is SOAKED -- even with two identical couples established, since caravans are not frequent there
R' Zeira resolves the baraita against the Gittin mishna with the same caravans distinction
version A: R' Zeira withholds return only where the two couples are established -- identical to Rabba
(within the disputing version) Rabba reads 'court enactments are returned' as found IN court -- a caravan-like venue -- so only הוחזקו blocks return
(within the disputing version) R' Zeira reads it as found OUTSIDE court; found inside, it would not be returned
R' Yirmeya: the found gett is returned where its witnesses attest they never signed another gett for a man of that name
Rav Ashi: returned where the loser gives a clear-cut mark -- a hole beside such-and-such a letter; a bare 'it has a hole' is not enough
are ordinary distinguishing marks effective by Torah law or by rabbinic law? (Rav Ashi's unresolved doubt; hence he trusts only a clear-cut mark)
